name: Cygnus Finance Global USD
oneLiner: cgUSD is Cygnus Finance's rebasing USD stablecoin on Base, backed by short-term U.S. Treasuries and stablecoins, with daily rebases reflecting NAV.
collateral: Short-term U.S. Treasury bills held off-chain, supplemented by on-chain stablecoins (USDC/USDT); supply rebases daily on New York banking days to match portfolio net asset value including accrued interest
pegMechanism: Daily rebase on NYC banking days aligning total supply with portfolio NAV; 1:1 USDC redemption via two-step withdrawal (request + claim, 5–7 day settlement); Transmuter enables instant 1:1 conversion between cgUSD and USDC; Elixir AMO manages on-chain liquidity

mechanismArchetypeReview.reviewer: SONG-5 Safety Score V9 mechanism review
mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Cygnus describes cgUSD as collateralized by short-term U.S. Treasuries, with total supply synchronized to portfolio net asset value on New York banking days and a 1:1 USDC redemption path. This is a Treasury-backed, NAV-rebasing stablecoin rather than a borrower-CDP or fiat cash-only issuance design.

mintAuthority.summary: cgUSD is an ERC-4626 rebasing vault on Base where users mint by depositing USDC/USDT (incl. cross-chain via Axelar), but Cygnus custodies the off-chain U.S. Treasury reserves, controls the daily oracle-reported NAV rebase, and runs an AMO managing on-chain liquidity. Both the vault and oracle are owned by a TimelockController with 10s delay, controlled by a 2/11 Safe as proposer.

sources.label: Cygnus cgUSD withdrawals FAQ (custodian T-bill sales)

reserveReview.rationale: Re-opened primary Cygnus docs on 2026-07-28. Overview still states that on each New York banking day cgUSD total supply is synchronized to portfolio NAV including off-chain U.S. Treasuries, on-chain stablecoins, and asset interest, with 1:1 USDC redemption support. How-it-works still defines the rebase NAV as on-chain stablecoins (C, labeled USDC in the US Treasury Asset Pool) plus market value of U.S. Treasury bills (T) and interest. Withdrawals FAQ independently states redemptions are fulfilled by selling U.S. Treasury bills held in a custodian account, converting USD proceeds to USDC for the asset pool (5–7 day settlement under normal conditions). DefiLlama's third-party cgUSD profile restates the same portfolio envelope (on-chain stablecoins, U.S. Treasury bill market value, accrued interest) without itemized weights. No attestation, reserve report, or itemized composition dashboard was found. At Base block 49201799, vault 0xca72827a3d211cfd8f6b00ac98824872b72cab49 totalSupply ≈ 76.17M cgUSD while its USDC balance was only ≈ 698.89 USDC — confirming that almost all backing is not held as USDC on the vault contract, but not establishing the off-chain T-bill vs stablecoin weights. Structural 100% multi-category basket with known-unknown disposition is therefore retained; no weight split was fabricated.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Cygnus issuer NAV portfolio description and redemption mechanics, re-opened 2026-07-28; DefiLlama catalog corroboration
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Current Treasury and stablecoin weights, holdings, reserve balances, named custodians, and independent assurance are not disclosed in the reviewed issuer or third-party sources.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-2 (lead buidl-blackrock)

sources.label: Cygnus cgUSD withdrawals FAQ (custodian-account T-bill sales)

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Cygnus documents that redemptions are fulfilled by selling U.S. Treasury bills held in a custodian account, but the custodian is never named and no segregation, bankruptcy-remoteness, or reuse terms are published; there is no reserve attestation from any accountant. On-chain, the cgUSD supply tracks an issuer-administered NAV oracle (vault and oracle governed by a 10-second timelock per the 2026-07-16 on-chain control review), so the reported off-chain portfolio value is issuer-asserted rather than independently fed.
